references.title: IFO-VGIC: Irregular Forced Opening of Voltage-Gated Ion Channels by electromagnetic fields
references.finding: Comprehensive review of 131 studies. 95% report oxidative effects from RF/Wi-Fi exposure. IFO-VGIC mechanism: polarized, coherent RF-EMF forces S4 voltage sensor to oscillate at non-physiological frequency, causing irregular channel opening, uncontrolled Ca2+ influx, ROS, DNA damage, sperm disorders, hormonal changes. VGIC blockers prevent effects, confirming mechanism.

references.authors: Bertagna F, Lewis R, McArthur S, Bhatt DK
references.title: Electromagnetic fields modulate neuronal membrane ionic currents through altered cellular calcium homeostasis
references.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
references.finding: 50 Hz, 1 mT, 60 min ELF-EMF on mouse hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons. Inward currents ↓40%, transient outward ↓50%. Two independent Ca²⁺ pathways identified: (1) RyR (ryanodine receptor) — dantrolene blocked EMF effects; (2) SERCA (sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca²⁺-ATPase) — CPA blocked EMF effects. Both intracellular Ca²⁺ store pathways abrogate EMF-induced ionic current changes, extending IFO-VGIC mechanism to include intracellular calcium dynamics.

references.authors: Koivisto M, Revonsuo A, Krause C et al.
references.title: Effects of 902 MHz electromagnetic field emitted by cellular telephones on response times in humans
references.finding: Two double-blind RCTs (2000a: n=48, 30 min; 2000b: n=48, 60 min). 902 MHz GSM left-sided exposure. Facilitation of cognitive performance (3-Back RT decrease in 2000a; Simple RT, Vigilance, Subtraction in 2000b). Compatible with acute VGIC activation at non-thermal SAR. Note: not replicated (Haarala 2003, 2005).

references.authors: Eliyahu I, Luria R, Hareuveny R et al.
references.title: Effects of radiofrequency radiation emitted by cellular telephones on the cognitive functions of humans
references.finding: n=36, 890.2 MHz, 2h bilateral exposure (Nokia 5110, 2W peak). Left-sided exposure slowed left-hand RT in spatial recognition task. Lateralization supports BERM two-channel spatial structure: EMF effect localizes to the exposed hemisphere. Compatible with local VGCC activation (pathway A) and local BBB opening (pathway E, cf. Salford 2003).

references.authors: Luria R, Eliyahu I, Hareuveny R et al.
references.title: Cognitive effects of radiation emitted by cellular phones
references.finding: n=48 right-handed males, 890.2 MHz, 1h, SAR 0.54-1.09 W/kg (Nokia 5110). Right-hand RT increased during left-sided exposure (first 2 blocks only). Time-dependent adaptation compatible with Selye GAS dynamics (alarm to resistance), which BERM pathway D (HPA to HPG) models at chronic timescale. Male-only sample matches BERM bioCap target population.

references.authors: Cadossi R, Massari L, Racine-Avila J, Aaron RK
references.title: Pulsed Electromagnetic Field Stimulation of Bone Healing and Joint Preservation: Cellular Mechanisms of Skeletal Response

references.title: Efficacy and Safety of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in the Acute Treatment of Major Depression

references.title: GammaCore non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation for migraine and cluster headache

references.title: Apparatus and method for electromagnetic treatment
references.finding: Patent explicitly states: 'electromagnetic field capable of eliciting a non-thermal biological effect in the treatment of infections.' PRF 27.12 MHz used clinically since 1960s for edema, wound healing, nerve regeneration.

references.authors: Zhao J, Xu L, Sun J, ym.
references.title: Global trends in incidence, death, burden and risk factors of early-onset cancer from 1990 to 2019

references.title: Global patterns and trends in colorectal cancer incidence in young adults

references.title: Cross Currents: The Perils of Electropollution, The Promise of Electromedicine
references.finding: Extended dual nervous system theory. Identified pineal gland as magnetic sensor. Showed melatonin secretion altered by magnetic fields at geomagnetic strength. Predicted chronic EMF -> chronic stress syndrome -> immune decline.

references.title: We Are Electric: Inside the 200-Year Hunt for Our Body's Bioelectric Code, and What the Future Holds

references.authors: Tinsley JN, Molodtsov MI, Prevedel R, Wartmann D, Espigulé-Pons J, Lauwers M, Vaziri A
references.title: Direct detection of a single photon by humans

references.title: Non-ionotropic voltage-gated calcium channel signaling
references.finding: VGCCs activate intracellular signaling pathways (gene transcription, synaptic transmission, cardiac contraction) through conformational change WITHOUT ion flux. Energy threshold is significantly lower than for ion flux, implying biological sensitivity to weaker fields than the ion-flux threshold would predict.

references.title: Honeybees' Behaviour in a Faraday-Shielded Hive: Mandatory Schumann Resonance for Colony Survival
references.finding: Faraday cage without Schumann resonance caused colony collapse — queens stopped laying fertilized eggs. Faraday + Schumann (7.83 Hz) restored colony survival. Bees need natural EM but are harmed by artificial EMF.

references.title: Static electricity passively attracts ticks onto hosts
references.finding: Electrostatic charge on hosts passively attracts ticks across air gaps. Mechanism likely applies to Varroa destructor.

references.title: Attraction of Varroa jacobsoni by electrical charges
references.finding: Varroa mite movement altered by charge sign of metallic lure mimicking bee charges. Establishes electrostatic host-finding.

references.title: Electromagnetic fields disrupt the pollination service by honeybees
references.finding: EMF disrupts honeybee foraging, navigation, and pollination through magnetoreception disorder. Gene and protein expression changes confirmed.

references.title: Exposure to 900 MHz EMF induces stress response in honeybees
references.finding: 900 MHz altered stress enzymes (AST, ALT, ALP) and stress gene expression (hsp70, hsp90, vitellogenin) in honeybees.

references.title: EMF shield for beehives
references.finding: Patent states: 'bees can better defend the colony against mites and hive beetles' when EMF blocked.

references.title: A Varroa destructor protein atlas reveals molecular underpinnings of developmental transitions

references.title: The Influence of an EMF at 900 MHz on the Behavior of a Honey Bee
references.finding: 50 Hz E-field reduced self-grooming, walking, and inter-individual contacts in honeybees. Grooming is primary Varroa defense.

references.title: Electric Entomology: How Insects Interact With Electricity
references.finding: Varroa mites increase activity in negative electric fields too weak to lift them. Flowers' charge acts as additional sensory signal for mite interception.

references.authors: Zeghoudi A, Bendaoud A, Canale L, Tilmatine A, Slimani H

references.finding: Direct measurement of LED driver near-field E-field emissions. Components decrease with distance but measurable at cm range. First systematic characterization of LED driver IF emissions.

references.title: CISPR 15: Limits and methods of measurement of radio disturbance from lighting equipment
references.finding: Recognizes LED driver PWM emissions at 50-200 kHz switching frequency. Standard designed for EMC (device interference), not biological safety.

references.title: Commission Regulation (EC) No 244/2009: Ecodesign requirements for non-directional household lamps

references.title: Keeping EMI from LED Drivers Under Control
references.finding: LED driver EMI 'can be extremely high.' Case: LED bulb interfered with garage door remote. Switch-mode PS generates conducted + radiated emissions at switching freq and harmonics.

references.title: 5G RF EMF Spectral Exposure Assessment in Four European Countries
references.finding: Spectral measurement of 5G RF-EMF exposure levels in four European countries. references.title: Why We Sleep: Unlocking the Power of Sleep and Dreams

references.title: Effect of 1 Week of Sleep Restriction on Testosterone Levels in Young Healthy Men

references.title: Why Sleep Is Important for Health: A Psychoneuroimmunology Perspective

references.authors: Spiegel, K., Leproult, R. & Van Cauter, E.

references.authors: Chang, A.M., Aeschbach, D., Duffy, J.F. & Czeisler, C.A.

references.authors: Duraccio, K.M., Zaugg, K.K., Blackburn, R.C. & Jensen, C.D.

references.authors: Clarke, D., Whitney, H., Sutton, G. & Robert, D.

references.finding: Bumblebees detect and learn floral electric fields. First demonstration of aerial electroreception in a terrestrial animal.

references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

references.title: Electric Fields Elicit Ballooning in Spiders
references.finding: Spiders detect electric fields via trichobothria and initiate ballooning. Atmospheric electric fields sufficient for spider dispersal. Electroreception extended to arachnids.

references.title: Aerial electroreception
references.finding: Review formalizing aerial electroreception as a recognized sensory modality in arthropods. Widespread across bees, flies, spiders, worms, caterpillars.

references.title: Caterpillars detect approaching predators via electric fields
references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
references.finding: Caterpillars detect approaching wasps via electric field and initiate defensive behavior before contact. Electroreception used for predator avoidance.

references.title: Electrostatic pollination by butterflies and moths
references.journal: Journal of the Royal Society Interface
references.finding: 269 butterflies/moths across 11 species: electrostatic charge varies with ecology. First evidence that electrostatic properties are adaptive traits shaped by natural selection.

references.authors: England, S.J., Lihou, K.L. & Robert, D.

references.authors: Belmin, C., Hoffmann, R., Pichler, P.-P. & Weisz, H.

references.finding: Electricity access is independently associated with fertility decline in DHS data across 44 countries, controlling for education and wealth. Confirms binary electrification threshold.

references.authors: Adey, W.R., Bawin, S.M. & Lawrence, A.F.

references.title: Acute low-intensity microwave exposure increases DNA single-strand breaks in rat brain cells
references.finding: 2450 MHz, 1.2 W/kg, 2h → DNA single-strand breaks in rat brain cells. Melatonin (antioxidant) prevented effect → ROS-mediated mechanism. Industry attempted suppression via counter-studies and university pressure.

references.title: Single- and double-strand DNA breaks in rat brain cells after acute exposure to radiofrequency electromagnetic radiation
references.finding: Both single and double strand DNA breaks in rat brain after 2450 MHz exposure. Confirmed and extended 1995 finding.

references.title: Adaptive evolution of voltage-gated sodium channels: the first 800 million years
references.finding: Voltage-gated ion channels conserved for >800 million years (3+ billion for ancestral forms). S4 voltage sensor is one of evolution's oldest molecular machines — optimized to quantum sensitivity limits.

references.title: Bibliography of Reported Biological Phenomena ('Effects') and Clinical Manifestations Attributed to Microwave and Radio-Frequency Radiation
references.finding: 2,300+ studies across 17 effect categories compiled by US Navy. Documented non-thermal biological effects decades before current debate. Subsequently largely forgotten in Western literature.

references.authors: Cipriani A, Furukawa TA, Salanti G, et al.
references.title: Comparative efficacy and acceptability of 21 antidepressant drugs for the acute treatment of adults with major depressive disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
references.finding: Network meta-analysis of 116,477 patients across 522 trials. All 21 antidepressants more effective than placebo. NNT ≈ 7 for SSRIs. Chemical (serotonergic) approach shows modest effect size.

references.authors: Goodwin GM, Aaronson ST, Alvarez O, et al.
references.title: Single-Dose Psilocybin for a Treatment-Resistant Episode of Major Depression
references.finding: Single 25mg psilocybin dose produced rapid, sustained antidepressant response in treatment-resistant depression. NNT ≈ 3. Effect within hours, sustained weeks. Demonstrates ionic reset mechanism superiority over chemical approach.

references.title: 5-HT2A receptor signaling converges on Cav1.2 (CACNA1C) calcium channels
references.finding: 5-HT2A → Gq → PLC → IP3 → Ca²⁺ ER release → CIF → Cav1.2 (CACNA1C) activation. Psychedelics target the same voltage-gated calcium channel that EMF modulates via VGCC mechanism. Provides molecular link between psychedelic efficacy and EMF biological effects.

references.title: Ion homeostasis and the mechanism of action of lithium

references.authors: Zarate CA Jr, Singh JB, Carlson PJ, et al.
references.title: A randomized trial of an N-methyl-D-aspartate antagonist in treatment-resistant depression
references.finding: First RCT of ketamine for depression. Rapid antidepressant effect within hours. NMDA receptor is an ion channel (Ca²⁺/Na⁺-permeable), not a neurotransmitter receptor. Demonstrates that depression responds to direct ion channel modulation.

references.authors: Rosenthal ES, Maguire CB, Bhatt DL, et al.
references.title: Electroconvulsive therapy generates a postictal wave of spreading depolarization in mice and humans

references.authors: Lim K, Halim A, Lu T, et al.
references.title: The skin battery: transepithelial potential in wound healing and regeneration

references.authors: Zhao M, Song B, Pu J, et al.
references.title: Electrical signals control wound healing through phosphatidylinositol-3-OH kinase-gamma and PTEN
references.finding: Endogenous wound electric fields (100–200 mV/mm) are the dominant directional cue for cell migration during wound healing, overriding chemical gradients. Genetic disruption of electrical signaling impairs wound healing more than disrupting chemical signaling.

references.title: On the piezoelectric effect of bone
references.journal: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan
references.finding: First demonstration of piezoelectricity in biological tissue (bone). The piezoelectric coefficient of collagen is 7–8 pC/N. references.authors: Skedung L, Arvidsson M, Chung JY, et al.
references.title: Feeling small: exploring the tactile perception limits

references.authors: Mohandas S, Bhatt K, Engel JL, et al.
references.title: PIEZO1 in keratinocytes: mechanotransduction and calcium signaling

references.authors: Chen Y, Fang Q, Wang Z, et al.
references.title: TRPV4 mediates histaminergic itch in keratinocytes
references.finding: TRPV4 is a multimodal ion channel in keratinocytes that responds to mechanical pressure, heat (>27°C), UVB, and osmotic pressure — all producing Ca²⁺ influx. references.authors: Kulkarni M, Trifunovic D, Schubert T, et al.
references.title: Calcium dynamics change in degenerating cone photoreceptors

references.authors: Bhatt DK, Bhatt K, Bhatt M.
references.title: Voltage-gated calcium channel subtypes in the retina

references.authors: Ouyang X, Yang J, Hong Z, et al.
references.title: Mechanisms of blue light-induced eye disease
references.finding: Blue light hazard operates through A2E photosensitization and direct mitochondrial ROS generation. references.title: Post-hospital syndrome — an acquired, transient condition of generalized risk

references.title: Electromagnetic fields in the intensive care unit
references.finding: ICU environment electromagnetic field measurements showed up to 40 µT near medical equipment. The study concluded 'ICU environment is at risk from electromagnetic pollution' and noted the long-term stay of critically ill patients in this environment.

references.title: Radiofrequency electromagnetic field exposure in hospital environments
references.finding: Modern hospital RF-EMF measurements across all frequency channels (ELF, IF, RF). Confirms continuous multi-channel EMF exposure in patient care areas from Wi-Fi, LED lighting, monitors, and medical devices.

references.title: Acute low-intensity microwave exposure increases DNA single-strand breaks in rat brain cells
references.finding: Low-intensity microwave exposure (2.45 GHz, 1 mW/cm², 2 hours) significantly increased DNA single-strand breaks in rat brain cells. This was one of the first studies showing non-thermal DNA damage from RF-EMF and became a target of industry-documented suppression efforts.

references.authors: Engels S, Schneider NL, Lefeldt N, et al.
references.title: Anthropogenic electromagnetic noise disrupts magnetic compass orientation in a migratory bird
references.finding: Broadband RF electromagnetic noise (50 kHz – 5 MHz) disrupts magnetic compass orientation in European robins via the radical pair mechanism (RPM) in cryptochrome. Faraday shielding restored orientation. This directly demonstrates that anthropogenic EMF disrupts CRY-based biological navigation.

references.title: Hospital-acquired disability in older adults: systematic review and meta-analysis
references.finding: Hospital-acquired disability (HAD) meta-analysis: 61× higher risk of ADL disability during hospitalization, 68% of elderly patients discharge below their admission functional baseline. These numbers exceed what bed rest and stress alone can explain.

references.title: Electromagnetic pulse opens blood-brain barrier tight junctions via conformational change without altering protein expression
references.authors: Gao M, Peng H, Hou Y et al.
references.finding: Electromagnetic pulse (EMP) caused BBB disruption in rat brains via tight junction protein (occludin, claudin, ZO-1) degradation. Note: EMP is high-amplitude short-duration, different from BERM's chronic low-intensity RF exposure. Mechanistic relevance: same molecular target (tight junctions) as Salford 2003 GSM study.

references.title: Scoping review: electromagnetic field effects on blood-brain barrier permeability
references.authors: IOP Science (Physics in Medicine and Biology)
references.finding: Evidence contradictory but positive results replicated in multiple independent labs (Salford, Tang, Ulusoy, Gao). Negative results partly explained by measurement method differences.

references.title: Short-term RF-EMF application as non-invasive tool for targeted BBB modulation
references.journal: Iranian Journal of Basic Medical Sciences
references.finding: RF-EMF (27.12 MHz) proposed as therapeutic BBB-opening tool for drug delivery. Mechanism: eNOS → NO → occludin downregulation. TDP variant.

references.title: Electromagnetic field treatment protects against and reverses cognitive impairment in Alzheimer transgenic mice
references.finding: 918 MHz EMF (2h/day) disaggregates Aβ oligomers, enhances mitochondria, reverses cognitive decline in AD mice. BBB opening beneficial in clean blood context.

references.title: Age-related changes in blood-brain barrier tight junction protein expression in mice
references.finding: Aged mice (24 months vs 3 months): occludin significantly decreased, ZO-1 decreased, TNF-α elevated in brain endothelial cells, capillary permeability significantly increased.

references.title: 900 MHz EMF exposure impairs spatial memory and increases BBB permeability in rats
references.finding: 900 MHz, 3h/day, 28 days → spatial memory impairment AND BBB permeability increase in rat hippocampus and cortex. Mechanism: mkp-1/ERK pathway. Below safety standards.

references.title: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi exposure affects brain microRNA expression below safety limits
references.finding: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi well below legal limit → significant changes in brain microRNA expression. Long-term 2.4 GHz exposure may lead to adverse effects including neurodegenerative diseases via miRNA changes.

references.title: Mobile phone radiation activates hsp27/p38MAPK stress response in human endothelial cells
references.finding: 900 MHz activates hsp27/p38MAPK stress response in human endothelial cells. Hypothesis: hsp27 activation may increase BBB permeability via endothelial stress fiber stabilization.

references.title: Calcium hypothesis of Alzheimer's disease and brain aging: A framework for integrating new evidence
references.finding: Ca²⁺ dysregulation is a PROXIMAL CAUSE of Alzheimer's dysfunction. Intracellular calcium changes precede and drive amyloid pathology, not the reverse.

references.title: Effect of calcium on Aβ(1-40) aggregation: toxic oligomers vs. harmless fibrils
references.finding: In the presence of Ca²⁺, Aβ(1-40) preferentially forms TOXIC OLIGOMERS rather than harmless fibrils. Calcium level determines whether amyloid is dangerous or not.

references.title: Alzheimer's disease: A short review of the role of calcium in early events
references.finding: Ca²⁺ dysregulation is an EARLY event in AD that precedes neurodegeneration. Calcium signaling changes occur before clinical symptoms.

references.title: Calcium homeostasis and neuronal excitability in Aβ neurotoxicity
references.finding: Ca²⁺ homeostasis and neuronal excitability are key factors in Aβ neurotoxicity. Disruption of calcium regulation amplifies amyloid toxicity.

references.title: Presenilin mutations and calcium dysregulation in Alzheimer's disease
references.finding: PSEN1/PSEN2 mutations (familial AD) cause Ca²⁺ dysregulation genetically. Demonstrates genetic convergence on the same calcium pathway that EMF activates environmentally.

references.title: Why anti-amyloid therapies have not lived up to their promise
references.finding: Anti-amyloid drugs remove plaques but do NOT improve cognition. Plaques are a symptom, not the cause. Need alternative mechanistic hypotheses for AD.

references.title: Prenatal exposure to magnetic field nonionizing radiation and the risk of ADHD in offspring
references.authors: Li DK, Chen H, Ferber JR, Hirst AK, Odouli R
references.finding: 1482 mother-child pairs with objective MF measurement (24h dosimetry). High prenatal MF → ADHD risk ↑, especially persistent/severe ADHD and ADHD with immune comorbidities. Dose-response relationship. Modifiable risk factor.

references.title: CACNA1C in psychiatric disorders: comprehensive review of GWAS associations
references.finding: CACNA1C rs1006737 repeatedly associates with bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, MDD, ADHD, and ASD in GWAS. Same gene/channel that modulates EMF sleep sensitivity (Sousouri 2025).

references.title: CACNA1C gene and vulnerability to neuropsychiatric disorders
references.finding: Comprehensive review of CACNA1C Cav1.2 role across psychiatric diagnoses. VGCC dysfunction is a convergence point for multiple neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders.

references.title: CACNA1C gain-of-function equivalent to Timothy syndrome alters axon targeting and behavior
references.finding: Timothy syndrome CACNA1C gain-of-function (G406R) causes autism with high penetrance. VGCC overactivity = autistic phenotype. Channel function directly regulates neural network development.

references.title: Alpha2A-adrenoceptors strengthen working memory networks by inhibiting cAMP-HCN channel signaling in prefrontal cortex
references.finding: Guanfacine mechanism: α2A → cAMP↓ → HCN channels close → membrane potential stabilized → PFC signal-to-noise ratio improves. Direct ion channel intervention for ADHD, not neurotransmitter modulation.

references.title: Fetal radiofrequency radiation exposure from 800-1900 MHz-rated cellular telephones affects neurodevelopment and behavior in mice
references.authors: Aldad TS, Gan G, Gao X-B, Taylor HS
references.finding: 800-1900 MHz fetal exposure in mice → neurodevelopmental and behavioral changes. Experimental confirmation of Kaiser Permanente epidemiological findings.

references.title: Prenatal mobile phone exposure affects cognition in aged rat offspring
references.finding: Prenatal mobile phone exposure → cognitive decline in AGED rat offspring. Effect is LIFELONG, not transient. Supports permanent calibration error hypothesis.

references.title: CACNA1A and autism spectrum disorders
references.finding: CACNA1A (P/Q-type VGCC) variants associate with ASD. Expressed in cortex, cerebellum, hippocampus. Multiple VGCC subtypes implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders.

references.title: Rare CACNA1H variants in autism spectrum disorder families
references.finding: 53 rare CACNA1H (T-type Cav3.2) variants identified in 40 ASD families. T-type calcium channel dysfunction contributes to ASD risk.

references.title: Involvement of voltage-gated calcium channels in early brain development
references.finding: VGCCs are critical for brain DEVELOPMENT, not just function. Channel expression regulates neural migration, synaptogenesis, and network formation during critical windows.

references.title: Ion channel conductance changes underlie bipolar neuron excitability oscillations
references.finding: Bipolar hippocampal neurons oscillate between hyperexcitability and hypoexcitability due to Na⁺ current decrease + K⁺ current increase. Li-responsive neurons are hyperexcitable (stable, correctable); Li-nonresponsive are UNSTABLE (oscillating).

references.title: Na,K-ATPase hypothesis of bipolar disorder
references.finding: MILD Na,K-ATPase dysfunction → excitability ↑ → MANIA. MORE SEVERE dysfunction → neurotransmitter release ↓ → DEPRESSION. Two levels of the SAME ionic disruption produce OPPOSITE clinical states.

references.title: Potassium channels in bipolar disorder
references.finding: Comprehensive review of K⁺ channel roles in bipolar disorder. Multiple potassium channel genes implicated in mood regulation and bipolar risk.

references.title: Leukemia cells hijack stromal cell bioelectricity via CaV1.2 depolarization
references.finding: Leukemia cells 'hijack' stromal cell bioelectricity through CaV1.2 depolarization. Direct evidence that cancer manipulates ion channel bioelectricity for survival.

references.title: Vagus nerve stimulation inhibits cytokine production and attenuates disease severity in rheumatoid arthritis
references.finding: VNS activates α7nAChR (ligand-gated ion channel) → NF-κB ↓ → TNF-α ↓ → significant response in rheumatoid arthritis. Direct ionic intervention for autoimmune disease.

references.title: Verapamil inhibits breast cancer cell growth in vitro
references.finding: Verapamil (VGCC L-type blocker) inhibits breast cancer cell growth in vitro. Ion channel modulation as anti-cancer strategy.

references.title: PI3K/AKT → GSK3β → KCNQ2 pathway in bipolar disorder
references.finding: PI3K/AKT → GSK3β → KCNQ2 signaling pathway links lithium's mechanism to potassium channel regulation in bipolar disorder.

references.authors: Tong J, Sheng S, Sun Y, et al.
references.title: Melatonin levels in follicular fluid as markers for IVF outcomes and predicting ovarian reserve
references.finding: Meta-analysis showing melatonin supplementation improves IVF fertilization rate, embryo quality, and clinical pregnancy rate

references.authors: Tamura H, Takasaki A, Taketani T, et al.
references.title: The role of melatonin as an antioxidant in the follicle
references.finding: Follicular fluid melatonin correlates with oocyte quality; melatonin acts as critical antioxidant protector of oocytes

references.title: Systematic review of melatonin effects on oocyte and embryo quality in IVF
references.finding: Systematic review confirms melatonin supplementation improves oocyte quality, embryo development, and IVF success rates

references.title: Meta-analysis of melatonin supplementation and clinical pregnancy rate in IVF
references.finding: Meta-analysis: melatonin supplementation significantly improves clinical pregnancy rate in IVF

references.title: Melatonin and female reproductive function: five mechanistic pathways
references.finding: Review: melatonin affects female fertility via HPG axis, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, mitochondrial, and epigenetic pathways

references.authors: Wilson BW, Anderson LE, Hilton DI, Phillips RD
references.title: Chronic exposure to 60-Hz electric fields: effects on pineal function in the rat
references.finding: ELF EMF suppresses nocturnal melatonin peak in rats via pineal gland pathway

references.authors: Reiter RJ, Tan DX, Manchester LC, et al.
references.title: Melatonin in reproduction revisited
references.finding: Melatonin protects sperm from oxidative damage, regulates HPG axis, and modulates seasonal reproduction

references.authors: Unfer V, Raffone E, Riber P, et al.
references.title: Effect of a supplementation with myo-inositol plus melatonin on oocyte quality in women undergoing IVF
references.finding: Melatonin + myo-inositol improves oocyte quality in IVF; small N, blinding challenges

references.authors: Nishihara T, Hashimoto S, Ito K, et al.
references.title: Oral melatonin supplementation improves human sperm motility
references.finding: Melatonin supplementation improves sperm motility in vitro and in vivo

references.title: Radiofrequency electromagnetic fields and melatonin: epidemiological review
references.finding: Review of RF-EMF and melatonin suppression in humans: inconsistent results, plausible mechanism

references.authors: Higuchi S, Motohashi Y, Ishibashi K, Maeda T
references.title: Influence of eye colors of Caucasians and Asians on suppression of melatonin secretion by light
references.journal: Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol
references.finding: Light-eyed Caucasians: 89% melatonin suppression. Dark-eyed Asians: 73%. Eye pigmentation directly modulates circadian light pathway.

references.title: Systematic review of intermediate frequency electromagnetic field animal studies
references.finding: IF range (300 Hz - 10 MHz) systematically under-researched compared to ELF and RF. Studies on health effects with more diverse perspectives of IF-EMF have NOT been conducted. Regulatory gap confirmed.

references.authors: University of the West Indies research group
references.title: Effects of 150 kHz intermediate frequency electromagnetic radiation on rat reproductive parameters
references.finding: 150 kHz IF-EMR 8 weeks: testicular mass decrease (p=0.03), interstitial cell count decrease (p=0.01), FSH increase (p=0.01), sperm trajectory changes (p=0.05). 150 kHz is within LED driver emission range.

references.authors: Kim J, Hwang Y, Kim S, Kwon D, Park J et al.
references.title: Electromagnetic field-inducible in vivo gene switch for remote spatiotemporal control of gene expression
references.finding: 60 Hz 2 mT pulsed EMF activates Lgr4 gene promoter in vivo via Cyb5b mitochondrial outer membrane protein producing rhythmic Ca2+ oscillations. CRISPR-identified mechanism. Reversible. Published in Cell (IF ~64). Contested by York (New Scientist): incredibly implausible.

references.authors: Duraccio KM, Zaugg KK, Langeveld RC, Jensen CD
references.title: Blue light filtering does not improve sleep outcomes in adolescents
references.finding: Blue-light-filtering glasses did NOT significantly improve adolescent sleep quality. Suggests non-optical component (IF emissions from screens/LED lighting) may be more important than blue light for sleep disruption.

references.title: Impact of electromagnetic fields on circadian rhythms: molecular and physiological insights
references.finding: PRISMA 2020 systematic review: 55 studies from 892 screened. 88% of high-quality animal studies report EMF-induced melatonin suppression (20-50% from baseline). Clock gene expression altered. Sleep architecture changes documented. Melatonin suppression smaller than light-induced (>90%). Only 27% of studies met high methodological standards.

references.title: Effect of iris pigmentation and latitude on chronotype and sleep timing
references.finding: Light-eyed subjects had earlier sleep times and more morningness. Iris pigmentation modulates circadian light sensitivity.

references.title: Dirty electricity, chronic stress, neurotransmitters and disease
references.finding: Library intervention: reducing kHz-range IF transients changed urinary dopamine and PEA in 7 volunteers. N=7 pilot, low evidence level, but mechanism consistent with IF affecting neurotransmitter pathway.

references.title: Dirty electricity elevates blood sugar among electrically sensitive diabetics
references.finding: kHz-range transients elevated blood glucose in electrosensitive diabetic patients. GS filters reduced both IF transients and blood glucose. Small N, controversial author. Mechanism consistent with K-ATP channel hypothesis.

references.title: Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) FDA approval for glioblastoma
references.finding: 200 kHz alternating electric fields disrupt mitotic spindle and destroy cancer cells. FDA-approved for glioblastoma (2011, 2015). Operating frequency (200 kHz) in same range as LED driver emissions (20-300 kHz). If 200 kHz intentionally disrupts cell division, environmental 200 kHz from LED drivers may do so unintentionally.

references.title: Fertility and ageing
references.finding: Comprehensive review of declining fertility trends across industrialized nations, documenting age-specific and cohort-specific fertility decline patterns

references.authors: Kirson ED, Dbalý V, Tovarys F ym.
references.title: Alternating electric fields arrest cell proliferation in animal tumor models and human brain tumors
references.finding: 100-500 kHz electric fields inhibit cancer cell proliferation in vitro and in vivo. Normal cell mitosis disrupted at ~50 kHz. FDA approval followed.

references.authors: Neuhaus E, Zirjacks L, Ganser K ym.
references.title: Alternating Electric Fields (TTFields) Activate Cav1.2 Channels in Human Glioblastoma Cells
references.finding: 200 kHz TTFields activate Cav1.2 (L-type VGCC) calcium channels in glioblastoma cells. Ca2+ entry, cell cycle arrest, mitochondrial membrane potential breakdown. Cav1.2 knockdown blunts effect. Same channel as Sousouri 2025 CACNA1C.

references.authors: Gera N, Yang A, Holber SC ym.
references.title: Mitotic Spindle Disruption by Alternating Electric Fields Leads to Improper Chromosome Segregation and Mitotic Catastrophe in Cancer Cells
references.finding: TTFields disrupt mitotic spindle via tubulin dimer dipole moment interference. Leads to chromosome missegregation and mitotic catastrophe. Mechanism: dielectrophoretic forces at cleavage furrow.

references.authors: Sato Y, Taki M, Kojimahara N
references.title: Association Between the Use of Induction Heating Cookers and Delivery Outcomes in Pregnant Women
references.finding: Statistically significant OR 1.27-1.44 for preterm birth with stationary/tabletop IH cookers. DOSE-RESPONSE: higher IF emission (9 mT) -> higher OR than lower (4 mT built-in). Internet-based cohort, Japan.

references.authors: Tokinobu A, Tanaka K, Arakawa M, Miyake Y
references.title: Maternal Use of Induction Heating Cookers During Pregnancy and Birth Outcomes: The Kyushu Okinawa Maternal and Child Health Study
references.finding: 1565 mothers, Kyushu cohort. IH cooker use associated with REDUCED preterm birth risk (contradicts Sato 2023). Difference likely due to IH type classification: Tokinobu did not separate high-emission vs low-emission cookers.

references.authors: Sato Y, Kiyohara K, Takehara S, Kojimahara N
references.title: Ecological study on the penetration of induction heating cookers and birth outcomes in Japan
references.finding: 47 prefectures. No significant association at ecological level. Weak positive association with fetal death after 22 weeks. Ecological design too coarse for individual-level exposure.

references.authors: Li DK, Odouli R, Wi S ym.
references.title: A population-based prospective cohort study of personal exposure to magnetic fields during pregnancy and the risk of miscarriage
references.finding: EMDEX-measured 24h MF exposure during pregnancy. Miscarriage risk doubled (OR ~2.0) above 1.6 mG. Dose-response relationship. Kaiser Permanente cohort.

references.authors: Li DK, Ferber JR, Odouli R, Quesenberry CP
references.title: A Prospective Study of In-utero Exposure to Magnetic Fields and the Risk of Childhood Obesity
references.finding: 733 children followed to age 13. Prenatal high MF exposure -> childhood obesity risk OR 1.69. 33 weight measurements per child on average. Kaiser Permanente.

references.authors: Li DK, Chen H, Odouli R
references.title: Maternal Exposure to Magnetic Fields During Pregnancy in Relation to the Risk of Asthma in Offspring
references.finding: Prenatal MF exposure associated with offspring asthma risk. EMDEX-measured. Kaiser Permanente cohort.

references.title: Exposure to magnetic fields and the risk of poor sperm quality
references.finding: Higher daily MF exposure >1.6 mG associated with 2-fold risk of poor sperm quality (abnormal motility and morphology). Dose-response relationship with duration.

references.authors: Khan MW, Roivainen P, Herrala M, Tiikkaja M, Sallmen M, Hietanen M, Juutilainen J
references.title: A pilot study on the reproductive risks of maternal exposure to magnetic fields from electronic article surveillance systems
references.finding: Finnish supermarket cashiers exposed to EAS (58 kHz). No significant differences in miscarriage, birth weight, or preterm birth. Could not differentiate EAS technology types. Authors recommend kHz-specific studies.

references.authors: Yamaguchi-Sekino S, Taki M, Ikuyo M ym.
references.title: Assessment of combined exposure to intermediate-frequency electromagnetic fields and pulsed electromagnetic fields among library workers in Japan
references.finding: EAS gates in libraries produce elliptically polarized IF magnetic fields. Chronic occupational exposure documented. Rotating fields may specifically affect melatonin.

references.title: Measurement and Exposure Assessment of Intermediate Frequency Magnetic Fields From Electronic Article Surveillance (EAS) Gates in Libraries
references.finding: Detailed IF-MF measurements from 5 EAS gate models. Transient and chronic exposure quantified. Induced electric field numerically calculated for human body models.

references.authors: Herrala M, Kumari K, Koivisto H ym.
references.title: Behavioral testing of mice exposed to intermediate frequency magnetic fields indicates mild memory impairment
references.finding: 7.5 kHz MF (EAS frequency), 120 uT, 5 weeks. Mild memory impairment in mice.

references.title: Early Exposure to Intermediate-Frequency Magnetic Fields Alters Brain Biomarkers without Histopathological Changes in Adult Mice
references.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
references.finding: 21 kHz 3.8 mT prenatal exposure -> NMDA receptor (NR1, NR2B), CaMKIV, CREB1, COX2, IL-1b, TNF-a, HO-1 all significantly increased in 7-week-old mice hippocampus. REVERSIBLE after exposure cessation.

references.title: Comparison of pulsed and continuous electromagnetic field generated by WPT system on human dermal and neural cells
references.finding: WPT system (87-207 kHz, 1.01-1.05 kW, 1.3-1.7 mT) tested on 4 human cell lines. Pulsed vs continuous exposure comparison.
